fullName.value: Tandem pore domain halothane-inhibited potassium channel 1

texts.value: K(+) channel that conducts outward rectifying tonic currents potentiated by purinergic signals (PubMed:24163367, PubMed:25148687, PubMed:30472253, PubMed:38409076). Homo- and heterodimerizes to form functional channels with distinct regulatory and gating properties (PubMed:25148687, PubMed:40011745, PubMed:40011746, PubMed:40307591, PubMed:40178898). Contributes most of K(+) currents at the plasma membrane of resting microglia (PubMed:38409076). Maintains a depolarized membrane potential required for proper ramified microglia morphology and phagocytosis, selectively mediating microglial pruning of presynaptic compartments at hippocampal excitatory synapses (PubMed:38409076). Upon local release of ATP caused by neuronal injury or infection, it is potentiated by P2RY12 and P2RX7 receptor signaling and contributes to ATP-triggered K(+) efflux underlying microglial NLRP3 inflammasome assembly and IL1B release (PubMed:38409076)

Activated by anionic lipids such as phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PI[4,5]P2 or PIP2) and oleoyl-CoA (PubMed:40011745). Activated by arachidonic acid (PubMed:30472253, PubMed:40307591). Inhibited by channel blocker tetrapentylammonium (PubMed:40307591). Inhibited by Ba(2+) ions, volatile anesthetics such as halothane and isoflurane, and antiarrhythmic drugs mexiletine and lidocaine (PubMed:30472253, PubMed:40178898). Insensitive to extracellular pH change (PubMed:24163367)
Homodimer (PubMed:40011745, PubMed:40011746, PubMed:40178898, PubMed:40307591). Heterodimer with KCNK12 (PubMed:25148687)

Each subunit contributes two pore-forming domains which assemble to form a single pore (PubMed:40011745, PubMed:40011746, PubMed:40178898, PubMed:40307591). The transmembrane helices are bridged by the selectivity filters 1 and 2 that coordinate the permeant ions (PubMed:40011745, PubMed:40011746, PubMed:40178898, PubMed:40307591). Up to four ions can simultaneously occupy the selectivity filter and at least two elementary charges must translocate across the filter to convert it into the open conformation (PubMed:40011745, PubMed:40011746, PubMed:40178898, PubMed:40307591)
Belongs to the two pore domain potassium channel (TC 1.A.1.8) family

features.description: Acts as a dominant negative when it assembles with wild-type KCNK13 or KCNK12 subunits, abolishing K(+) flux.

Increases channel basal activity. Increases the current amplitude. Confers nonlinear I-V relationship, with currents that saturate upon strong membrane depolarization; when associated with D-139. Does not affect channel ion selectivity, pH sensitivity nor inhibition by halothane.
